predecessors.name: Hittite Empire
predecessors.text: the south-east of the Hittite Empire: Carchemish and the Syro-Hittite lands

successors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
successors.text: the Syro-Hittite states, subdued by Assyria in the 8th century BCE; Carchemish conquered by Sargon II in 717

ledger.x: c. 1180 BC: Carchemish under Kuzi-Teshub carries on the Hittite crown after the fall of Hatti. The Carchemish page (reopened 2026-10-19) has Kuzi-Teshub, son of Talmi-Teshub, who 'claimed the title of "Great King" after the fall of Hatti', and dates the polity 'from c. 1175 to 975 BC'; the Hittites page has Hattusa…

c. 868 BC: Carchemish pays tribute to Assyria. Sangara (870-848) 'paid tribute to Kings Ashurnasirpal II and Shalmaneser III of Assyria' as 'a tributary probably at some time before 868 BC' (Carchemish page, reopened 2026-10-19); the page names Carchemish alone, and the rest of the -900 hull is the Cliopatria shape…
717 BC: the last Neo-Hittite kingdom falls.
717 BC: the tributary status ends with Sargon II's conquest of Carchemish ('conquered by Sargon II in 717 BC in the reign of King Pisiri'); the cells pass to Assyria in the loss below.

wars.name: Assyrian tribute demands on Carchemish (Ashurnasirpal II and Shalmaneser III)
Tiglath-Pileser III's conquest of Arpad and Pattin
wars.outcome: Arpad captured in 740 after a three-year campaign (743–740) and its lands made two provinces; Pattin annexed in 738 and the provinces of Kullania, Hatarikka and Simirra created; Gurgum, Kummuh, Carchemish and Quwê paid tribute afterwards.

wars.name: Sargon II's conquest of Carchemish
wars.outcome: Carchemish conquered in 717 BC during Pisiri's reign; the city becomes Assyrian, with a provincial capital at Til-Barsip.

certainty.note: Small kingdoms with no treaty or survey line; the Cliopatria shape is a rough hull around the Syro-Hittite cities, and the southern Aramean kingdoms inside it are not separated.
